newsitem.title: USA: Bill to prohibit foreigners from buying guns in US.
newsitem.headline: Bill to prohibit foreigners from buying guns in US.

text.p: A bill to prohibit foreign tourists from buying guns in the United States was introduced in the Senate on Thursday in response to Sunday's deadly shooting at New York's Empire State Building.

One person was killed and six others wounded on the building's observation deck when Palestinian Ali Abu Kamal opened fire with a semiautomatic handgun he bought last month in Florida. Kamal then killed himself.

Kamal, who came to the United States on Dec. 24, used his motel receipt in Melbourne, Florida, as proof of residency to obtain a Florida identification card. He used the card to buy the weapon at a nearby gunshop.
Kamal was given a criminal background check before he was allowed to buy the gun, but there was no information available about him because he had just come to the United States.
Democratic Sens. Edward Kennedy of Massachusetts and Richard Durbin of Illinois said the bill they introduced would close the loopholes in current law that allows foreign tourists to buy guns.

"There is virtually nothing to stop a terrorist from entering the United States on a tourist visa and then purchasing a supply of weapons legally in the United States for use in a terrorist activity," Kennedy said in a statement.
"There is no legitimate reason someone who is in the United States temporarily should be able to purchase or carry a firearm here," he added.

The Kennedy-Durbin bill would prohibit foreigners in the United States on non-immigrant visas from possessing firearms. Exceptions would be made for diplomats, hunters or marksmen taking part in shooting competitions.
